text: Why is gas five dollars and two cents in America...
but just one dollar in Kuwait?
There are three reasons. And number one is crazy.
Reason number three: taxes.
Every time Doug fills up in America, the government takes a cut.
Eighteen cents a gallon goes to Washington.
Then his state takes about thirty cents more.
In Kuwait? Zero gas tax. Zero.
That is about fifty cents on every gallon.
Reason number two: who owns the oil.
In America, oil companies own it.
They sell it at the world price, and they want profit.
So when oil goes up, your gas goes up.
In Kuwait, the government owns the oil. All of it.
And there are over one hundred billion barrels under the sand.
And only about five million people live there.
Reason number one: the government pays for your gas.
The real price of a gallon is way higher.
But the government pays the difference...
so the driver pays one dollar.
That costs Kuwait billions of dollars every year.
Sounds perfect, right? Here is the twist.
America pumps more oil than any country on Earth.
More than Kuwait. More than Saudi Arabia.
And Doug still paid five dollars a gallon.
Doug confused.
Because America sells its oil at the world price too.
At that price, one full tank costs seventy-five dollars in America...
and fifteen dollars in Kuwait.
That is sixty dollars back in your pocket.
Would you move to Kuwait for cheap gas? Comment below.
